q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE AS E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE AS E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPLOYEE_ID, NAME, EXPERIENCE_YEARS) VALUES (1, 'John Doe', 10); INSERT INTO PROJECT (PROJECT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) VALUES (1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses an INNER JOIN, which means it only considers projects that have at least one employee assigned to them. On the other hand, Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN, which means it considers all projects, including those without any assigned employees, and assigns NULL for the employee's experience years in such cases.
counterexample_dsp: A project with no assigned employee triggers the difference.
